headline: Darrius Missed The Median By Four Cents. DK Metcalf Scored 0.7 At Flex.
kicker: (122.20 against a 122.24 line. Alvin Kamara scored 6.7 on his bench. Metcalf caught one ball for two yards.)
lede: The line was 122.24. Nishil scored 122.28 and Darrius scored 122.20. Four cents above, four cents below, the closest the median has been all season (Week 3 split it 0.26 both ways). Darrius started DK Metcalf ($19) at flex: one catch, two yards, 0.7. Alvin Kamara scored 6.7 on his bench. Swap them and he clears it by almost six. He lost to Barrett too, 0-2. Nishil lost to Greg (Miley) by 10.02 and got a win from the median for four cents. Jon scored 70.80, the second-lowest score of the season behind his own 68.94, with a perfect lineup for the fourth week running, and Tom beat him by 75.56. Barrett is 20-2 and has never lost to the median. Chris is 19-3 and lost to it by 4.60 with Tyler Shough on his bench. Will went from 174.40 to 89.66. And Justice Hill, added by Maclane three times this season and benched every time, got dropped, claimed by Nishil for $3, started, and scored 15.6.
tldr: Darrius missed the median by 0.04. DK Metcalf ($19) started for 0.7. Kamara 6.7 on the bench.
Nishil cleared it by the same 0.04, lost his game, and went 1-1 anyway.
Jon: 70.80, a perfect lineup, 0-13. Fourth straight 100 percent week.
Maclane dropped Justice Hill. Nishil paid $3 and started him: 15.6. Maclane has lost five straight.
Barrett: 20-2, 11-0 against the median. His $1 bye-week quarterback scored 22.22.

sections.awards: Fourteen teams, fourteen awards. Nobody walked.
sections.power: Season to date. Best lineup is your record if you had started your best possible lineup every week. The tax is the wins you left on your own bench.
sections.median: Week 11's line was 122.24. Nishil cleared it by 0.04 and Darrius missed it by 0.04, the closest split of the season. Nishil lost his game and got a win here; Chris won his and lost here by 4.60. Six teams swept, six got swept. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 11 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Three perfect lineups: Anuj at 144.06, Will at 89.66 and Jon at 70.80.
sections.bench: 82.56 points of lineup regret, down from 126.14. Maclane leads with 18.06, most of it KaVontae Turpin.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 11, audited. $48 spent on 33 adds. The two biggest bids, $8 each: Mark Andrews 2.4, the Chiefs 9.06. A $6 claim started and scored zero.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. Brock Purdy: $3, 230.16 points. A.J. Brown: $45, 18.3, and zero more this week.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 11 against what Yahoo expected. Jonah Coleman beat his projection by 17.31. Ja'Marr Chase missed his by 14.19.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

games.note: Four cents. Nishil lost this game and won the week's closest argument anyway. Justin Herbert, the Monday pickup he benched last week for 16.26, started and threw two touchdowns and ran one in: 22.44. George Pickens 21.3, DJ Moore 19.1, Cam Little 13.4. Then Justice Hill. Maclane added him three times, benched him three times, and cut him. Nishil claimed him at 3:51 on Friday morning for $3 and started him: 69 yards, a touchdown, 15.6. Six adds this week, 49 moves, tied with Andrew for the most in the league. Emari Demercado ($6) and Kalif Raymond were both gone before Sunday. 122.28, 0.04 over the line, 1-1. Greg (Miley) started Jared Goff over Bryce Young again, right again: 20.36 to 16.96. Javonte Williams 22.6, Tetairoa McMillan 16.1, and the 49ers, picked up for nothing on Thursday night, scored a touchdown: 16.14. 132.30, 2-0, and he still has $90 of FAAB. He has spent $10 all season. His best-lineup record is 16-6. His real one is 9-13. That gap, seven wins, is the biggest in the league.

Barrett's quarterback was on bye, so on Wednesday he paid $1 for Cam Ward. Ward threw two touchdowns and ran one in: 22.22. The Bears ($4) scored 16.58. Chuba Hubbard ran for two touchdowns, 27.0. Evan Engram was added at 12:17 on Sunday and started: 10.4. Ladd McConkey 18.2. The one miss: Ja'Kobi Lane, a $6 claim, started and did not record a stat. 134.70, 2-0, 20-2, 11-0 against the median. Darrius lost by 12.50 and then lost the median by four cents. Travis Kelce caught two touchdowns, 22.4. C.J. Stroud ($1) 21.46. Then flex: DK Metcalf, $19, one catch for two yards, 0.7. Keenan Allen 5.3 at the other flex. On the bench: Kamara 6.7, Pat Freiermuth 6.5. The best lineup scores 129.70 and goes 1-1. 122.20, 0-2. He is 91-52 in all-play, third in the league, and 5-6 head to head.

Ashton Jeanty caught 90 yards and ran for 79: 25.4, 13.99 over his projection. Mike Evans 20.9. Saquon Barkley 13.5. Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions, 14.74. On Wednesday Abhishek added the Cowboys and benched them: 10.68 on the bench while the Bengals started for 7.1. Chig Okonkwo 8.6 on the bench, Isaiah Likely 4.0 at tight end. Tank Dell, flex, 5.2. Patrick Queen ($1) 3.5. 127.14, 2-0. Nathan solved the Kirk Cousins file again: benched him for 8.4, started Jayden Daniels for 17.06. Then he benched the Broncos, who scored a touchdown, 16.86, and started the Colts for 7.54. CeeDee Lamb 25.7. Emeka Egbuka ($25) 2.8. Tyler Warren 2.7. 111.30, 0-2, two straight losses, $0 of FAAB.

Last week Josh Allen outscored Tyler Shough and the note said Chris made the right call. This week Allen threw two interceptions for 14.16 and Shough scored 15.28 on the bench. Jahmyr Gibbs ran in two, 25.8. Malik Nabers 15.0, Tony Pollard 12.0. Wil Lutz and Elic Ayomanor, both added Wednesday morning, started: 8.8 and 4.2. The Steelers ($3) 11.68. 117.64, 1-1, missed the median by 4.60. The best lineup clears it by 0.30. Still 19-3, 10-1 head to head, $86 left. Will scored 89.66 a week after 174.40. Same Joe Burrow, 19.9. Same Christian McCaffrey, 13.2 after 46.3. Ja'Marr Chase ($63) caught five for 31 yards, 5.6, 14.19 under projection, the worst start of the week. Josh Downs started this time, 7.9. Gunnar Helm, added Friday, 2.4 at tight end. A perfect lineup. Last week his bench held 194.64. This week his best possible lineup was the one he played, and it went 1-12 in all-play. Down six.

Last week Greg (IR) started Jalen Coker and Germie Bernard for 1.3 combined. This week he benched them: Coker 6.7, Bernard 7.0. He started Jordyn Tyson (1.5) and Kyle Monangai (1.8) instead. Wrong both weeks, in opposite directions. It did not matter. Jonah Coleman, a $1 auction back, ran for 111 yards and three touchdowns: 33.9, 17.31 over projection, the best start of the week against projection. Brock Purdy ($3) threw three more, 22.2. Tyler Bass kicked 165 yards of field goals, 18.5. Mark Andrews, the $8 claim, 2.4. 127.18, 2-0, two straight. Maclane has lost five straight. KaVontae Turpin, the $0 claim he benched last week for 2.72, scored a rushing touchdown and returned 134 yards on the bench: 16.46. Ryan Flournoy started at wide receiver for 1.6. Jonathan Taylor ($62) 4.7. Garrett Wilson 5.4, DeVonta Smith 6.6. 18.06 points of regret, the most in the league, 83.3 percent, the worst efficiency in the league. And Justice Hill scored 15.6 for somebody else. 90.32, 0-2. Down four.

Anuj started Emmett Johnson for the second straight week, and this time it counted: 105 rushing yards, a touchdown, 23.3. Dak Prescott threw four touchdowns and ran in another: 35.9, the best start of Week 11. Bucky Irving 17.5, Jameson Williams 17.3. The Chiefs ($8) 9.06, Caleb Downs ($3) 6.0 at IDP. Mike Gesicki, $21 two weeks ago, 10.2 at flex after 3.5 in his first two starts. A perfect lineup, 144.06, 12-1 in all-play, 2-0. Up four. Andrew made five adds, down from sixteen. Michael Mayer, a $0 claim, started at tight end: one catch, four yards, 0.9. Mike Washington Jr., added Friday, 4.2 at running back. Luther Burden 3.3. Dohnte Meyers was added at 10:50 on Monday morning and scored 8.9 on the bench. Antonio Williams 17.7 and Chimere Dike 16.38 tried. 97.90, 0-2, two straight losses, and still fifth.

The biggest win of the week and the second biggest of the season, 75.56. Patrick Mahomes ($3) threw for 324 yards and three touchdowns, 24.96. The Texans allowed under seven points: 17.32. Breece Hall 17.5, Derrick Henry 17.1, Chris Olave 16.7, Khalil Shakir 13.8. Samaje Perine, added Thursday, 12.2 on the bench. 146.36, the high score, 13-0 in all-play, 2-0, 97.5 percent. Jon scored 70.80. Two starters scored zero: Courtland Sutton and Juwan Johnson. Jaylen Warren 3.9. Chase McLaughlin, added at 5:32 on Thursday morning, kicked three extra points: 3.0. And it was a perfect lineup, 100.0 percent, the fourth week in a row, for the same reason as last week: every player on the bench scored zero. A.J. Brown, Tyler Higbee, Bijan Robinson, Deshaun Watson, Dontayvion Wicks. 0-13 in all-play, 1-10 against the median, 4-18.
